none.name: Invisible Hat
none.description: It's like you're wearing nothing at all!

top-hat.name: Top Hat
top-hat.description: The mark of a true gentlebird.

viking-helmet.name: Viking Helmet
viking-helmet.description: Sure, vikings never actually wore this style of helmet, but why let facts get in the way of good fashion?

cowboy-hat.name: Cowboy Hat
cowboy-hat.description: You can't jam with the console cowboys without the appropriate attire.

fez.name: Fez
fez.description: It's a fez. Fezzes are cool.

wizard-hat.name: Wizard Hat
wizard-hat.description: Grants the bearer terrifying mystical power, but luckily birds only use it to summon old ladies with bread crumbs.

baseball-cap.name: Baseball Cap
baseball-cap.description: Birds unfortunately only ever hit 'fowl' balls...

flower-hat.name: Flower Hat
flower-hat.description: To be fair, this is less of a hat and more of a dirt clod that your pet happened to pick up.

beanie.name: Beanie
beanie.description: Keeps feathers warm on those long migrations south!

sun-hat.name: Sun Hat
sun-hat.description: Perfect for frolicking through enchanted flower fields.

straw-hat.name: Straw Hat
straw-hat.description: A classic design, though keep away from water as this particular hat is seemingly unable to float.

cordovan-hat.name: Cordovan Hat
cordovan-hat.description: A traditional Spanish hat that stays put even in the wildest of sword fights.

bluebird.name: Eastern Bluebird
bluebird.description: Native to North America and very social, though can be timid around people.

shimaEnaga.name: Shima Enaga
shimaEnaga.description: Small, fluffy birds found in the snowy regions of Japan, these birds are highly sought after by ornithologists and nature photographers.

tuftedTitmouse.name: Tufted Titmouse
tuftedTitmouse.description: Native to the eastern United States, these birds are full of personality, and notably my wife's favorite bird.

europeanRobin.name: European Robin
europeanRobin.description: Native to western Europe, this is the quintessential robin. Quite friendly, you'll often find them searching for worms.

redCardinal.name: Red Cardinal
redCardinal.description: Native to the eastern United States, this strikingly red bird is hard to miss.

americanGoldfinch.name: American Goldfinch
americanGoldfinch.description: Coloured a brilliant yellow, this bird feeds almost entirely on the seeds of plants such as thistle, sunflowers, and coneflowers.

barnSwallow.name: Barn Swallow
barnSwallow.description: Agile birds that often roost in man-made structures, these birds are known to build nests near Ospreys for protection.

mistletoebird.name: Mistletoebird
mistletoebird.description: Native to Australia, these birds eat mainly mistletoe and in turn spread the seeds far and wide.

scarletRobin.name: Scarlet Robin
scarletRobin.description: Native to Australia, this striking robin can be found in Eucalyptus forests.

americanRobin.name: American Robin
americanRobin.description: While not a true robin, this social North American bird is so named due to its orange coloring. It seems unbothered by nearby humans.

carolinaWren.name: Carolina Wren
carolinaWren.description: Native to the eastern United States, these little birds are known for their curious and energetic nature.

blackCappedChickadee.name: Black-capped Chickadee
blackCappedChickadee.description: Native to North America, these small and curious birds are known for their distinctive call from which they get their name.

blueJay.name: Blue Jay
blueJay.description: This loud and rambunctious bird is native to North America and is known for challenging anything in its path.

darkEyedJunco.name: Dark-eyed Junco
darkEyedJunco.description: Native across North America, these social birds will often be seen hopping along the ground in winter.

houseFinch.name: House Finch
houseFinch.description: Native to North America, these highly social birds sing cheerful songs and are often seen at bird feeders.

redWingedBlackbird.name: Red-winged Blackbird
redWingedBlackbird.description: Native across North America, these birds can be seen flocking in massive groups. Their songs are often heard in wetlands around the continent.

pigeon.name: Rock Pigeon
pigeon.description: Descended from the Rock Dove, these once domesticated birds are often found in cities worldwide. Quite friendly and intelligent, they were favored companions of Nikola Tesla.

redAvadavat.name: Red Avadavat
redAvadavat.description: Native to India and southeast Asia, these birds are also known as Strawberry Finches due to their speckled plumage.

pinkRobin.name: Pink Robin
pinkRobin.description: Native to Australia, these bubblegum-pink puffballs are quieter than most, instead relying on their vibrant colours to attract partners.

spangledCotinga.name: Spangled Cotinga
spangledCotinga.description: This South American bird can be found in the Amazon rainforest, flashing its iridescent turquoise feathers high above in the canopy.

elegantEuphonia.name: Elegant Euphonia
elegantEuphonia.description: This vividly coloured finch is found throughout Central America and is known for the distinctive blue hood that crowns its head.

paintedBunting.name: Painted Bunting
paintedBunting.description: A remarkably colourful bird, this North American species is quite difficult to observe despite its vivid palette due to its shy nature and vulnerable habitat.

redWarbler.name: Red Warbler
redWarbler.description: Endemic to the highlands of Mexico, this bird has the rare distinction of being one of the very few toxic birds in the world.

cubanTody.name: Cuban Tody
cubanTody.description: As the name suggests, this little green bird is only found on the island of Cuba and is known for being particularly round.

violetBackedStarling.name: Violet-backed Starling
violetBackedStarling.description: Native to Sub-Saharan Africa, these small starlings are known for being the most vividly purple birds in the world.

stellarsJay.name: Steller's Jay
stellarsJay.description: Native to western North America, I've always appreciated the coincidence of this bird's name and its deep blue plumage resembling the night sky.

mourningDove.name: Mourning Dove
mourningDove.description: Native to North America, this dove always reminds me of sunny mornings and warm summer days.

whiteWingedFairywren.name: White-winged Fairywren
whiteWingedFairywren.description: Native across Australia, these birds are known for their spectacular lapis lazuli coloured feathers and contrasting white wings.

littleCrow.name: Little Crow
littleCrow.description: Native to Australia, this species of crow is the smallest in the world, but no less clever than its larger siblings.

redpoll.name: Redpoll
redpoll.description: Native to the Arctic, this incredible bird is capable of withstanding temperatures as low as -65 degrees Fahrenheit (-54 Celsius).

invisible.name: Invisible
invisible.description: An unusual species, this bird is rarely seen.

pride.name: Pride
pride.description: A rather brightly colored bird with a global distribution, this species is known to allow a variety of birds to join its flock.

trans.name: Trans
trans.description: A pastel coloured bird with a global distribution, this species is known for its remarkable ability to adapt.

pidgey.name: Pidgey
pidgey.description: Native to Japan, these birds are known for their ability to fly long distances while carrying objects as heavy as a ten year old child.
